summary: This is a curated, professional analysis of installed packages on your system that are redundant, obsolete (due to transitioning from a MacBook Air laptop to a high-performance desktop), or specialized utilities that can be safely removed to eliminate bloat and free up space without causing any system instability.

laptop_to_desktop_obsolete.description: Packages that are obsolete or unnecessary after migrating from a portable MacBook laptop to a dedicated desktop system.

packages.name: preload
packages.reason: A daemon that monitors application launches and pre-loads binaries into unused RAM. While useful on older, slow laptop HDDs, it is completely obsolete on modern desktops with high-speed PCIe NVMe SSDs, where it only wastes background CPU cycles.

packages.name: upower
packages.reason: Daemon for power management. Crucial on laptops to track battery levels and handle lid-closure events, but only minimally useful on desktops for tracking peripheral (wireless mouse/keyboard) battery levels. If you do not use wireless peripherals, it can be safely removed.

redundant_hardware_info_and_system_monit.description: Multiple redundant applications installed for viewing hardware specifications, sensors, or diagnostics.

packages.name: hardinfo2
packages.reason: Graphical hardware information and benchmark tool. Redundant as you already have hwinfo, lshw, glances, inxi, btop, and fastfetch installed.

packages.name: glances
packages.reason: CLI system resource monitor. Heavily redundant since you have 'btop' installed (which is highly optimized and more feature-rich).

packages.name: hwinfo
packages.reason: Low-level hardware information gathering tool. Redundant with inxi, lshw, and fastfetch.

packages.name: lshw
packages.reason: List hardware utility. Redundant with inxi, hwinfo, and fastfetch.

packages.name: freeipmi
packages.reason: IPMI monitoring library. Intelligent Platform Management Interface (IPMI) is exclusively used on enterprise server-grade motherboards. It is completely useless on consumer desktop hardware like your ASRock B760 motherboard.

packages.name: ipmitool
packages.reason: Enterprise server IPMI CLI utility. Completely useless on a consumer desktop system.

packages.name: tmon
packages.reason: Kernel thermal monitoring tool. Highly redundant with the simpler and cleaner 'lm_sensors' (sensors command).

packages.name: turbostat
packages.reason: Intel CPU C-state and frequency reporting tool. Useful only for precise kernel core tuning/debugging; redundant for general desktop use.

redundant_web_browsers.description: Multiple heavy web browsers installed concurrently, which consume substantial disk space for updates and cache.

packages.name: ungoogled-chromium-bin
packages.reason: An ungoogled version of the Chromium browser. Redundant given that you already have Google Chrome and Zen Browser installed.

packages.name: tor-browser-bin
packages.reason: Tor Browser. Only necessary if you require onion-routed anonymous web browsing.

virtualization_and_emulators.description: Heavy virtualization packages that consume substantial disk space and load system modules (like kvm/tun/tap) if you are not running local virtual machines.

packages.name: qemu-system-x86
packages.reason: Full system x86 emulator. Extremely heavy package, only needed if you are running local VMs via libvirt/VirtualBox.

packages.name: virt-manager
packages.reason: Graphical GUI manager for KVM/QEMU virtual machines. Redundant if you do not run local VMs.

packages.name: libvirt
packages.reason: Virtualization management API and daemon. Redundant if you are not hosting VMs on this desktop.

redundant_text_and_ide_editors.description: Multiple redundant text/document editing software and IDE variations.

packages.name: vscodium-bin
packages.reason: Telemetry-free build of VS Code. Highly redundant because you have the official VS Code ('code') package and 'antigravity-ide' both installed.

packages.name: cherrytree
packages.reason: Hierarchical node-based text editor. Highly redundant if your primary note-taking app is Obsidian.

specialized_development_and_wasm_librari.description: Very specialized toolchains and compiler runtimes that are unnecessary unless you are actively developing WebAssembly or testing legacy Python applications.

packages.name: python311
packages.reason: Older standalone Python 3.11 build. Arch Linux's default system python is 3.13+, meaning python311 is redundant unless you run a legacy script that fails on newer python versions.

packages.name: wasi-compiler-rt
packages.reason: WebAssembly compiler runtime from LLVM. Highly specialized WASM development library.

packages.name: wasi-libc
packages.reason: C library headers for WebAssembly systems. Only useful for native-to-WASM compiling.

packages.name: wasi-libc++
packages.reason: C++ standard library for WebAssembly. Highly specialized.

packages.name: wasm-bindgen
packages.reason: Rust WebAssembly binding generator. Specialized developer tool.

packages.name: wasm-pack
packages.reason: Rust WASM pack and packaging engine.

packages.name: wasm-tools
packages.reason: Low-level WebAssembly binary parsing and formatting tools.

redundant_benchmarks_and_stress_testers.description: Heavy benchmarking packages and system loaders.

packages.name: unigine-valley
packages.reason: Extremely heavy 3D GPU graphics benchmark (1.5+ GiB). Useful for a one-time GPU stress test or score comparison, but purely dead weight once testing is done.

packages.name: stress-ng
packages.reason: System load stress-tester. Only necessary for debugging CPU/RAM stability under maximum stress.

packages.name: systester
packages.reason: Multi-threaded Pi calculation benchmark. Redundant.

specialized_networking_and_scanning.description: Specialized administrator tools or duplicate network scripts.

packages.name: ssh-audit
packages.reason: SSH server security auditing utility. Redundant unless you are hardening remote SSH servers.

packages.name: ssh-tools
packages.reason: Assorted SSH helper scripts. Redundant for standard desktop needs.

packages.name: speedtest++
packages.reason: C++ CLI internet speed tester. Redundant because you already have 'speedtest-cli' installed.

assorted_unused_utilities.description: Auxiliary utilities that are typically unused unless specifically needed.

packages.name: bleachbit
packages.reason: Disk space cleaner. Often redundant with manual cache clears (like 'paccache') and logs cleanup; can sometimes delete important caches if configured incorrectly.

packages.name: rpi-imager
packages.reason: Raspberry Pi OS writing tool. Completely unused unless you actively flash SD cards for Raspberry Pi boards.

packages.name: tesseract-data-eng
packages.reason: English language dictionary and model files for Tesseract OCR. Redundant unless you run optical character recognition software locally.
